subject: Re: Deployment path for transaction inference — prioritization: latency vs throughput
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex@fastledger.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fastledger.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T15:03:00Z
Subject: Deployment path for transaction inference - decision inputs

Olga / Redwood team — thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our side to help narrow the path:

- Our core concern is p95 infer latency for single-transaction scoring during checkout — target <= 120ms (we'd like to get close to 80–100ms ideally).
- Peak throughput looks like ~350 qps over a 10-minute burst with steady-state 60–90 qps.
- Traffic profile: 70% short prompts (~30 tokens), 30% longer contextual prompts (up to 200 tokens) when fraud review kicks in.
- Data residency: must remain in us-east; we may eventually evaluate VPC for full separation (compliance team will flag).

Questions: given our latency target and burst pattern, do you recommend starting dedicated or will hosted API with autoscaling + cold-start controls suffice? Also can you share a rough cost delta for a Dedicated pool sized for 350 qps burst vs expected hosted spend?

Attaching a small SLO table and sample QPS histogram.

—Alex
Senior Product Manager
FastLedger
Attachment: fastledger-slo-table.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@fastledger.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-22T18:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment path for transaction inference - decision inputs

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Recapping our read and recommended next steps so we can keep the decision simple: 

1) Quick read: your p95 target (<=120ms, ideal 80–100ms) + 350 qps burst points strongly toward Dedicated as the initial production mode, primarily because: 
   - Dedicated gives predictable GPU-resident KV caching and consistent batch sizing under burst, which materially reduces p95 variance.
   - For workloads with mixed short/long prompts our runtime can pin KV cache on a warm fleet; hosted autoscaling can meet average qps but may add tail latency during sudden bursts.

2) Hosted as a pilot: we recommend beginning with a short Hosted pilot for functional validation (1–2 weeks, traffic-shadowed or throttled to 50–100 qps) while we size a Dedicated pool. This minimizes time-to-value and uncovers prompt-level regressions.

3) Sizing guidance (initial estimate): to hit p95 ~100ms for 30-token prompts and sustain 350 qps bursts with <5% token-queueing, we'd target a Dedicated pool equivalent to ~6x A100-class GPUs (we'll firm this up with perf tests).

4) Cost delta: very roughly, Dedicated committed rate (monthly) will be ~2.3–2.8x net of hosted pay-as-you-go for your burst profile, but unit-cost/token will be lower and latency predictable — we'll provide a modeled comparison by EOD tomorrow.

5) Compliance / VPC: Private VPC is optional as a follow-on (post-production launch) — not required to hit latency targets but useful for audit/audit-logs and KMS controls.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood runs two quick perf tests we discussed (synthetic QPS + replay of your sample histogram) — target: measure p95 and required concurrency.
- Ben to propose exact Dedicated GPU mix and run cost model.
- Schedule a 45-min architecture session with your infra/security folks to cover VPC/KMS needs.

Can you confirm a preferred 45-min slot next week? I'll coordinate the test plan once you confirm.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-arch-sketch.pdf (diagram)
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, Alex Ruiz <alex@fastledger.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-22T19:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment path for transaction inference - technical sizing notes

Alex / team — quick technical note to add to Olga's summary:

- Latency drivers: model size and attention recomputation under variable context lengths. For ~30-token prompts a properly warmed KV cache and small batch windows (continuous batching disabled for latency paths) should let us reach ~80–110ms p95 on A100-class instances.
- For the 200-token contexts during fraud review, expect token generation time to increase; we'll capture that in the perf run and recommend a readthrough policy (route long-context requests to a slightly larger instance type or a separate Dedicated lane).
- Warm-up and prefix-caching: We'll instrument prefix-hit rates in the pilot and add an autoscale policy that favors kept-warm pods during expected burst windows (if you have hour-of-day patterns we can lock warm capacity).

I will run an initial cluster sizing sweep tonight and deliver a recommended Dedicated configuration and a comparison cost spreadsheet by tomorrow AM. If you can share a 48-hour raw traffic replay (anonymized) it will make the sizing faster — otherwise we'll use the histogram you attached.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@fastledger.com>, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2027-09-23T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment path for transaction inference - prioritization: latency vs throughput

Alex — following up to lock calendar and scope:

- Proposed 45-min slot: Tue 2027-09-28 16:00–16:45 ET — Infra + Security + Product. Please confirm or suggest alternatives.
- Deliverables before the call: Ben's Dedicated sizing + cost model, Olga's perf-test plan, and a short checklist for the security session (VPC/KMS/audit logs).
- Ask from you: if possible, upload the 48-hour anonymized replay to the Drive link I shared; if not, confirm that we should proceed with the histogram.

Once we confirm, we'll run the Hosted pilot (shadow mode at 50 qps) while we run perf tests to finalize Dedicated sizing. From there we can set a go/no-go for Dedicated commit within 2 weeks of the perf results.

Quick FYI: if you prefer a phased Dedicated approach we can start with a smaller committed baseline (3–4 GPUs) plus a burst buffer — that can accelerate launch and reduce upfront commit.

Thanks and cc'ing the infra/security alias for visibility.

—Marissa Cole
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
